spec.name: Blend v36
spec.notes: Combined signal, rebalanced on a slow schedule.

claim.text: Research-period backtest: Sharpe 2.4, annual return 8%, maximum drawdown 4%.

exhibits.summary: Delaying the signal by 1 more bar moves the Sharpe ratio from 2.40 to -0.48 (change -2.88). The strategy already trades a bar after its signal, so this measures how fast the signal fades, not look-ahead.
Under strict point-in-time data the Sharpe ratio moves from 2.40 to 2.40. Strict mode changed no field or operator the signal uses.
At 10 bps the Sharpe ratio is -0.97 (as submitted, 0 bps: 2.40); it breaks even at 7.1 bps with daily turnover 0.43.
On the full universe the Sharpe ratio is 2.40 against 2.40 as submitted; the strategy never saw 0 delisted assets.
On the sealed period, traded as live (strict data, 10 bps, at least one bar of lag), the Sharpe ratio is -1.45 against 2.40 in research, a gap of +3.85.
The best year gives 16% of total P&L (year 2) and calm regimes give 85%; Sharpe is 3.48 in calm and 0.98 in stressed regimes.
The log holds 2 distinct specs; the best of 2 under no edge is expected to reach a Sharpe of 0.17, so the claimed 2.40 becomes 2.23 and the probability that the true Sharpe is above zero is 100%.
The real signal's gross Sharpe of 2.38 beats 100% of 200 shuffled signals (shuffled mean 0.02, 95th percentile 0.54).
Perturbing the 3 numeric values in the signal by up to 50% moves the Sharpe ratio from 2.40 to as low as 1.85 (as low as 2.28 at 25%).
The top 1% of days (23 days) give 24% of total P&L and the top 5 assets give 17% (net of the strategy's own costs).

series.label: cumulative share of P&L, best days first
